methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $50M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Isembard is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Alexander Fitzgerald that has raised $50M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for post-money valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $100M. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector comparables spanning Series B and Seed stages, with valuations ranging from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B), producing a median of $1.7B.

These methods imply a wide valuation range of $85M to $2.0B, with a midpoint of $900M. The substantial dispersion reflects material stage and maturity differences within the peer set: the Stage-progression method is anchored to disclosed raise data but likely underweights the market's valuation of frontier robotics capabilities, while the Peer-median result reflects comparables predominantly at Series B, one stage ahead. Key uncertainties include revenue traction, technical differentiation relative to peers, and capital efficiency. A refined estimate would benefit from revenue multiples or ARR data if available, and narrowing the peer set to Series A equivalents.
